setting.era: It is 1912. Think and speak like someone of that time: no later words, objects or ideas.
setting.gm: A lighthouse on Grey Rock, a bare island off the coast of Maine, in October 1912. Kerosene lamps, a clockwork-turned lens, a telegraph only on the mainland. A storm is building: wind rising, sea getting up. Nothing supernatural happens. The scene builds toward nightfall, when the lamp must be lit.
setting.known: You live on Grey Rock, a lighthouse island two miles off the coast of Maine, in the autumn of 1912. The supply boat comes from Port Clyde once a fortnight. The nearest neighbors are on the mainland.

boat_landing.name: boat landing
boat_landing.desc: Slick granite steps down to a timber landing, waves slapping at the pilings. A rope rail leads up to the keeper's house.

keepers_quarters.name: keeper's quarters
keepers_quarters.desc: A low kitchen with an iron stove, a scrubbed table, a lamp on a hook and oilskins dripping by the door. A shelf holds the station logbook. A narrow door leads to the tower stairs, another to the oil store.

oil_store.name: oil store
oil_store.desc: A brick room that smells of kerosene. Rows of oil cans, spare wicks, a workbench with lamp parts.

tower_stairs.name: tower stairs
tower_stairs.desc: An iron spiral staircase climbing the inside of the tower. Every step rings underfoot.

lamp_room.name: lamp room
lamp_room.desc: A glass-walled room at the top of the tower around the great Fresnel lens and its kerosene lamp. Wind moans around the gallery outside.

oil_key.desc: Brass key to the oil store, on a nail-chain in Jonah Price's waistcoat pocket.

logbook.desc: The station logbook. Entries in Keeper Hale's hand say the light burned all night every night this month.

watered_oil.desc: Three oil cans at the back that have been cut with water. Lamp oil from them sputters and dies after an hour or two.
watered_oil.find: INT -2 when examining the oil cans

letter.desc: A letter in a tobacco tin wedged under the bottom landing step: 'Dark on the 14th and 28th, same as before. Usual pay. - M.'
letter.find: WIS -4 when searching the landing steps

lantern.desc: A hand lantern on a hook by the door.

truth: Jonah Price is paid by a rum-runner called Marsh to let the light fail on agreed nights so boats can land unseen on the mainland shore.
Jonah makes the light fail by filling the lamp from watered oil cans he keeps at the back of the oil store.
The instructions come in letters left in a tobacco tin under the bottom step of the boat landing. The latest says the light must go dark tonight, the 14th.
Keeper Hale knows the light has failed twice this month, but he fell asleep on watch both times and wrote in the logbook that it burned all night.

player.name: the inspector
player.appearance: a man in a wet Lighthouse Service greatcoat
